messages.subject: Problem with Editing Command Line after Switching Windows
messages.subject_clean: Problem with Editing Command Line after Switching Windows
messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

I recently downloaded Seewave and am in the process of learning it, in the hopes of using it for an upcoming research project.

Unfortunately, it seems that every time I switch windows (i.e. ALT + TAB) to another program, e.g. to double-check how to correctly word an argument/function, when I switch back to R it doesn't allow me to edit the command line anymore. I've since started doing the bulk of my editing in Notepad++, but it's still somewhat annoying.

Has anyone else experienced this problem? Would very much appreciate help.

I am running it on Windows 7, on the most recent packages of r and Seewave.

Thanks!

-Alex

messages.subject_clean: [seewave] Problem with Editing Command Line after Switching Windows
messages.body_plain:
Hi Alex,

This is likely an R problem, rather than a seewave problem.

I'm not sure why you're running into that problem, but I would highly recommend downloading RStudio (https://www.rstudio.com/). It's a program that makes working with R much much easier! It'll keep track of you your R commands (.R file, like your Notepad) as well as the R console (like your R) all in the same place and you can use buttons or keyboard shortcuts to send commands from the script to the console. Much easier than copy and pasting from Notepad. And hopefully shouldn't give you issues when you use Alt + Tab.

Good luck!

Steffi

messages.subject_clean: [seewave] Re: finding pitch of recorded human Speech using fundamental frequencies from autoc()
messages.body_plain:
I'm sorry I never used that function in seewave. Probably is a well optimized procedure to get the pitch by cepstrum. However, optimal pitch extraction usually requires a well adapted set of parameters to match voice features also in relation to the used sampling frequency. The cepstrum is usually the best tool to separate voiced and unvoiced sounds. To extract formants for both, and to find pitch for voiced sounds only. Also, if you use a short enough window on the signal, you can easily track pitch changes related to emotional expression and prosody

Gianni.

messages.subject: Nosie reduction / Filters
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

We made an experiment in natural environment to study sound detection, localization and propagation.

We installed a microphones array of 20 automatic recording units and we played a synthetic sound (mixed pure tones, with fundamental frequencies ranging from 300 to 1000 Hz).

We are now looking for an algorithm for noise reduction (for example median noise filter).

After much research, I unfortunately don’t found automated methods to reduce background noise.

I found some Matlab scripts and I would like to know if similar scripts or functions exist with Seewave or R.

I would be very grateful if you have any advice for me.

Best regards,

Morgane PAPIN
